appBuilderComponents.name: ERP Integration

setupSteps.label: Confirmed status
setupSteps.title: Create the "Confirmed in ERP" order status
setupSteps.why: Without it, an order the ERP confirmed looks the same as one it never saw in the Orders grid.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Order Status: create erp_confirmed, assign it to Pending (not as default), then pick it for "Order status when the ERP confirms" on the integration's Mapping tab.
setupSteps.then: Assign it to Pending (not as default), then pick it on the integration's Mapping tab.

setupSteps.label: Shared catalogs
setupSteps.title: Give each priced company its own shared catalog
setupSteps.why: The ERP publishes a company's prices into that company's shared catalog; companies sharing one would share prices.
setupSteps.where: Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog, then Assign Companies.
setupSteps.then: Assign the company under Assign Companies.

setupSteps.label: Price scope
setupSteps.title: Set the catalog price scope to Website
setupSteps.why: The ERP publishes a company's prices per website; at the default scope, Global, every site would show the same prices. No API sets this.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Price > Catalog Price Scope: set to Website, Save Config. Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Set Pricing and Structure then shows a Website chooser above the prices.

setupSteps.label: ERP warehouse
setupSteps.title: Give each ERP a warehouse, and assign it to the website's stock
setupSteps.why: Each ERP keeps stock per Commerce source (a warehouse). The Default Stock can hold only the Default Source, so the website needs a stock of its own.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Inventory > Sources > Add New Source, one per ERP (for example Northwind Warehouse); Stores > Inventory > Stocks > Add New Stock with the website as its sales channel and the warehouses assigned; then move the website's products' quantities to the new source (Catalog > Products > Actions > Move stock between the ERP's warehouses) and save each product once, so the storefront's catalog reads the new stock.
setupSteps.then: Add a stock for the website and assign the warehouses to it, move the products' quantities to them, and save each product once.

setupSteps.label: Product attributes
setupSteps.title: Create the erp_owner and brand product attributes
setupSteps.why: A product goes to the ERP its erp_owner names (the ERP's list id: its name in lower case without the word ERP — Accuform ERP is accuform); a product with no erp_owner stays with the ERP that owns everything. brand is what buyers filter on.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Attributes > Product > Add New Attribute: erp_owner as a Text Field (a Dropdown sends a number, not the id) and brand; then Stores > Attributes > Attribute Set to add both to every set your products use (the check names any set erp_owner is missing from, and Demo Builder can add it). Give each additional ERP its products with Assign products on its card, and set brand on the products you sell.
setupSteps.then: erp_owner is a Text Field in every attribute set your products use; a value for an attribute not in a product's set is dropped without an error. Give each additional ERP its products with Assign products on its card; untagged products stay with the ERP on everything.

setupSteps.label: Partially Held status
setupSteps.title: Create the "Partially Held" order status
setupSteps.why: When one ERP holds its part of an order and another carries on, the order says so; without it the integration writes only a note.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Order Status: create partially_held (label Partially Held), then assign it to Processing and to Pending (not as default, not visible on the storefront).
setupSteps.then: Assign it to Processing and Pending (not as default, not visible on the storefront).

setupSteps.label: Payment on Account
setupSteps.title: Switch on Payment on Account for the website
setupSteps.why: Company buyers pay against the company's credit line, which the ERP credit story needs.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Payment on Account, at the website's scope: untick Use Default beside Enabled, set Enabled to Yes, Save Config.
setupSteps.then: At the website's scope, untick Use Default first, then Save Config.

setupSteps.label: Returns
setupSteps.title: Switch on returns for the storefront
setupSteps.why: A buyer asks for a return on the storefront, and the integration sends each ERP its lines of it. With returns off, staff can still enter a return in the Admin, but the buyer cannot ask for one.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Configuration > Sales > Sales > RMA Settings: set Enable RMA on Storefront to Yes, Save Config.
setupSteps.then: Leave Enable RMA on Product Level at Yes so every product can be returned, and Save Config.

setupSteps.label: Card payments
setupSteps.title: Switch on card payments for the storefront
setupSteps.why: Only for a demo where the buyer pays by card. Payment Services is Commerce's own card payments, powered by PayPal, and needs its own sandbox onboarding with a PayPal sandbox business account before it can be switched on.
setupSteps.where: Sales > Payment Services: click Sandbox onboarding and connect a PayPal sandbox business account, then under Settings > General Configuration, for the website, set Enable to Yes and Save.
setupSteps.then: Finish Sandbox onboarding first, and keep Payment mode at Sandbox so no real card is charged.

appBuilderComponents.description: Connects Commerce to an ERP: orders, prices and stock stay in sync.
